The agent makes load and first-token time much faster across the shipped file formats, using mmap, lazy paging, layout changes and parallel conversion.

facts.claim: PR #613 exists in ggml-org/llama.cpp, titled 'Make loading weights 10-100x faster', by jart with slaren credited, and it is merged into master (merge line visible, dated 2023-03-30).
PR #613 changes the weight file format so tensors are memory-mapped instead of read and copied, with 32-byte tensor alignment and split-file merging in the converter.
The PR's merge commit SHA and the exact pre-PR parent commit (the claimed base) are identified.
Smoke-build commit 4a45de4f is the pre-PR-613 base the seed says it pins to.
Current master still implements mmap, madvise (posix_madvise WILLNEED/RANDOM, MADV_WILLNEED prefetch) and mlock in src/llama-mmap.cpp, so the successor design is public and in the current tree.
Upstream's 10-100x speedup claim for the loader change.

full_card.band: 4 h tier. Frontier agent reaches mmap quickly; remaining credit is conversion and parallelism. Weaker model breaks alignment. No dated public evidence.
full_card.build_cost: Smoke build 361 s green; trimming the snapshot and writing the harness is about 2-4 days. Estimated build cost band 4.
full_card.deliverable: Faster load and first-token time across shipped formats via mmap, lazy paging, layout changes and parallel conversion, with identical tensor checksums.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Checksum gate on fresh hidden files; page-cache-aware harness to stop cached-tensor and checksum shortcuts. Cold-cache control under gVisor is unproven.
full_card.grading_surface: Tensor checksums on fresh hidden synthetic model files across formats and shapes (gate), then wall-clock medians of cold and warm loads vs reference speedup S.
full_card.local_fit: Builds offline (smoke green, 361 s build). gVisor mmap and cold-cache control are the risk; no root drop_caches assumed.
full_card.lookup: direct: the reference change is merged public history and its successor code (llama-mmap.cpp) is in current master; mmap-for-weights is textbook.
full_card.provenance: llama.cpp PR #613 'Make loading weights 10-100x faster' (jart, slaren), merged 2023-03-30, MIT; base = pre-PR parent (SHA not confirmed).
full_card.reference: Upstream mmap loader change, trimmed and re-measured by the pipeline; claim of 10-100x is unverified.
full_card.ships: Trimmed pre-PR-613 snapshot of the read-and-copy GGML model loader plus a CLI that loads a synthetic model file and runs a checksum pass. History-less snapshot required.
full_card.similarity: Neighbours S-op-002 (0.342) and S-op-001 (0.253) are above the 0.15 novelty threshold; both are unknown sibling seeds, not verified public tasks. Not a near-duplicate of a public task on inspection.

v1.kill_reason: One-lever: the seed itself says mmap is the lever a frontier agent reaches, leaving only conversion and parallelism as partial credit on a 4 h tier. Also at risk: K8 (mmap is recallable from the public merged PR and current master) and K4 (cold-cache timing unproven under gVisor). The base pin is also unconfirmed.

Band.why: No dated public evidence; the seed's own description says mmap is reached easily and only conversion/parallel credit remains, so 3 max without evidence.

Build.why: Smoke build green in 361 s; snapshot trimming and harness are a few days.

Fit.why: Offline build works, but gVisor mmap behaviour and unreachable cold-cache state weaken timing.

Hor.why: One dominant lever (mmap) and a 4 h tier; the work is not long-horizon.

Lic.why: MIT, which allows shipping the snapshot and reference.

Multi.why: Format variants give some buckets, but the main speedup is one lever, so credit is lumpy.

Nov.why: Two neighbours above 0.15 (0.342, 0.253) from sibling seeds on the same llama.cpp subject; not a listed public task.

Real.why: Merged upstream PR #613 with MIT licence and a real codebase.

Ref.why: Upstream change is real and public, but the 10-100x claim is unverified and the trimmed reference still needs measuring.

Seal.why: Reference design is public in merged history and current master; the synthetic hidden files are sealable, but the approach is recallable.

Surf.why: Checksums over a handful of formats and shapes; probably tens to low hundreds of hidden cases, not thousands.

spike_plan.kill_if: Trivial mmap gets at least 90% of the reference speedup (one-lever, too easy), or the base and reference cannot be separated by timing noise, or the parent SHA cannot be confirmed.
spike_plan.pass_if: Pre-613 parent confirmed; checksums identical across builds; reference warm-load speedup at least 3x the base with run-to-run spread under 20%; cold-cache control works or is dropped with a stated fallback.
steps: Clone the repo in a throwaway container with network; check out the parent commit of PR #613 and confirm it is the pre-613 base; record the SHA.
Build the pre-613 loader snapshot and the reference (merged PR state) with cmake; note build time and whether the smoke suite result matches.
Write a small generator for synthetic GGML files in two or three formats/shapes and compute tensor checksums with both builds; confirm identical checksums.
Time load of the base and the reference with 5+ repeats each, warm cache; record median and the ratio.
Test whether cold cache can be controlled in this gVisor-like setup (writable /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches or equivalent); if not, drop the cold-load measurement from the design.
Check run-to-run variance across 5 runs; check that a trivial mmap-only implementation gets most of the reference speedup.

v1.summary: PR #613 ("Make loading weights 10-100x faster", merged 2023-03-30, MIT) is real and its successor mmap code is public in current master, so the lookup is direct and the mmap lever is recallable. The seed is one-lever on a 4 h tier with unproven cold-cache timing, so I kill it as K10 (with K8/K4 risk) unless the scope is widened to a multi-lever optimization.
